run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-17T09:44:24Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Within the observable telemetry (traces ~08:53–09:05Z, metrics ~09:02–09:14Z on 2026-11-17), every error-status span attributed to fraud-detection is a gRPC client call to flagd: 4 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and 1 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt, while its own Kafka consumer operations (orders process 12, orders receive 10) carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET. In the fully read trace bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05 the fraud-detection client span lasts 599,999,905 µs and ends with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) as parent of a flagd server span (service flagd, v0.12.8) whose otel.status_description is exactly "stream closed due to server-side timeout"; 10 such EventStream client spans (~594–602 s each) were returned for 08:53–09:04. The only flagd workload is Deployment flagd (1/1 ready, pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx, restartCount 0, no stream-timeout flag in its start arguments), and the same flagd EventStream error counters also appear for ad (7) and recommendation (7), so the stream teardown originates on the flagd side rather than in fraud-detection's pods. fraud-detection was not crashing (10/10 pods Running, ready, 0 restarts) and its Kafka consumer spans show no errors; Kafka pod restarts (lbw2w 3, vg9vr 1, exitCode 1) predate the observable window and are not tied to the error spans. The conclusion is partial because the RequestErrorRate rule is not present in this Prometheus, no metric or trace sample exists after ~09:14Z (nothing at 09:44:24Z), and the observed error ratio reads 0 from 09:04:24Z to 09:09:24Z, so the alert's exact 0.0222 reading at 09:44:24Z could not be reproduced.

claims.text: At 09:15Z, fraud-detection's span-metric counters show 4 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and 1 STATUS_CODE_ERROR on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt, while its own operations orders process (12) and orders receive (10) carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET; all observed error spans of this service are gRPC client calls to flagd.

An error-filtered Jaeger sample (biased, not a failure rate) returns 10 fraud-detection client spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with status tags error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4, durations 594.1 s to 601.8 s, starting between 08:53:01Z and about 09:04Z.

Trace bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05 contains the fraud-detection client span (599,999,905 us, error, rpc.grpc.status_code=4) with a CHILD_OF-referenced flagd server span (service flagd, service_version v0.12.8, 553,397,947 us, error, rpc.grpc.status_code=4) whose otel.status_description is exactly "stream closed due to server-side timeout".

Deployment flagd has 1 replica, ready 1, available 1; its single pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx runs container flagd with image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8 and command /flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json (no stream-timeout or deadline argument), is Ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState.

The same flagd EventStream error signature is counted for other callers at 09:15Z: ad has 7 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (plus 17 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean) and recommendation has 7 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream.

Observability coverage is limited to roughly 09:00-09:14Z: count(traces_span_metrics_calls_total) evaluated over 08:44:24Z-09:57:32Z returns points only from 09:02:24Z (378 series) to 09:14:24Z (420 series), and the fraud-detection error-ratio expression (sum(rate(error[5m]))/sum(rate(all[5m]))) reads 0 at 09:04:24Z through 09:09:24Z and NaN from 09:10:24Z.

The events returned for namespace otel-demo (28 events, timestamps 09:03:43Z-09:06:47Z) concern HorizontalPodAutoscaler warnings (FailedGetResourceMetric/FailedComputeMetricsReplicas because the resource metrics API was unavailable, HPA postgres FailedGetScale x61), recommendation scale-down (Deployment recommendation ScalingReplicaSet 10->8->7, ReplicaSet recommendation-5f45f75855 SuccessfulDelete) and Pod Killing; none of the returned events names fraud-detection or flagd.

All 12 flags in ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) have defaultVariant "off" at query time, including adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure; this is the ConfigMap state at query time (~09:58Z), not proof of its state during the incident.

fraud-detection itself was not failing at pod level: Deployment fraud-detection reports 10 replicas, 10 ready and 10 available, and all 10 fraud-detection pods are phase Running with ready=true and restartCount 0.

Kafka instability is not the cause of fraud-detection's error spans: kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w (restartCount 3, last termination exitCode 1 reason Error at 08:59:47Z) and kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr (restartCount 1, exitCode 1 at 08:54:50Z) restarted before the observable error window and are now Running/Ready, and fraud-detection's Kafka consumer spans orders receive and orders process carry no error status.

The nonzero fraud-detection error rate is produced by flagd tearing down the long-lived flag evaluation EventStream: the client span ends at about 600 s with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and the fully-read trace attributes the close to "stream closed due to server-side timeout" on the flagd server span, so a recurring stream teardown of this kind is enough to keep an error-rate-above-zero alert firing even though no order processing operation of fraud-detection fails.

A second, unconfirmed candidate error source is the single STATUS_CODE_ERROR span on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt counted for fraud-detection; no error-tagged trace for that operation was returned by Jaeger, so it could be a flag-resolution failure distinct from the EventStream timeout or a by-product of the same connection teardown.

Review the flagd Deployment's gRPC evaluation-stream lifetime/keepalive behavior (no stream-timeout argument is set in its start command) and confirm whether the ~10-minute server-side stream closure is intended; if it is periodic expected behavior, add tolerance to the RequestErrorRate rule (e.g. ignore DEADLINE_EXCEEDED on the long-lived flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream) rather than treating every teardown as an error.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned nothing), so the expression, window and threshold that produced "current: 0.02222222222222222" are unknown and could not be reproduced.

Prometheus samples in this target stop at about 09:09-09:14Z and Jaeger traces stop at about 09:05Z, so the state at the alert start 09:44:24Z (and whether the same flagd EventStream errors continued) is unobserved; the observed error ratio is 0 at 09:04:24Z-09:09:24Z, followed by no data.

No telemetry before ~08:44Z (Jaeger error spans first appear at 08:53:01Z, span metrics at 09:02:24Z), so there is no baseline to say when the flagd server-side stream timeouts began or whether they are new.

Container logs were empty/unavailable for flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx (flagd, flagd-ui, init-config current and previous) and for fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l (fraud-detection, wait-for-kafka), so application-side messages about the stream teardown could not be read.

flagd-config is only observed at query time (~09:58Z) with all flags "off"; its state during the incident is unknown, and the change_history integration is not available, so no record of configuration or deployment changes exists.
Queries for NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota objects in otel-demo returned nothing, so their absence during the incident cannot be confirmed.
Kubernetes events cover only 09:03:43Z-09:06:47Z; events for fraud-detection or flagd outside that range, if any, are unknown.
next_steps: Retain and inspect the RequestErrorRate rule definition (expression, window, threshold) from the Alertmanager/Prometheus instance that fired it.
Collect Prometheus and tracing data for 09:14Z-09:57Z to verify whether fraud-detection's error rate at 09:44:24Z was still produced solely by flagd EventStream DEADLINE_EXCEEDED spans.
Check flagd's gRPC evaluation stream lifetime/keepalive documentation and configuration for v0.12.8 to confirm whether a ~550-600 s server-side stream close is expected.

Compare the same flagd EventStream error counters for ad and recommendation over the same window to decide whether the RequestErrorRate rule needs a stream-teardown exclusion rather than a per-service investigation.
